name: Mobile app and API
summary: A React Native app built with Expo (Flutter is the listed swap) talking to a typed API with Postgres, push notifications and offline caching on the device.

fitsWhen.says: the product is a mobile app
it needs a phone app or offline use
the team writes TypeScript or Dart

avoidWhen.says: it is content or data work
search ranking matters more than an app

mobile.why: One TypeScript codebase for iOS and Android, managed native modules and over-the-air updates.

backend.why: A typed API with an OpenAPI document the app's client is generated from.

database.why: System of record on the server.

cache.why: Rate limits and push notification queues.

queue.why: Push notifications and emails outside the request.

auth.why: Phone, email and social sign-in with tokens the API verifies.

ci-cd.why: API checks in CI; app builds and store submission through EAS.

observability.why: Crash reports from the app and errors from the API in one place.

testing.why: End-to-end tests on simulators; pytest for the API.

hosting.why: The app ships through the stores; the API runs on a managed platform.

services.name: api
responsibilities: Sends push through Expo's push service

environments.name: dev
environments.purpose: Expo Go or a dev build against a local API

environments.name: staging
environments.purpose: An internal build (TestFlight / internal testing) against the staging API

environments.name: prod
environments.purpose: Store releases against the production API

stages.name: test
stages.does: jest for the app, pytest for the API

stages.name: submit
stages.does: eas submit to the stores after review

notes: API as a container; the app has no servers of its own

security.auth: Short-lived access tokens with refresh tokens in the device's secure storage
security.secrets: No secrets inside the app bundle; everything secret stays on the API
notes: Certificate pinning only if the threat model needs it
Validate every request on the API; the app can be modified

folderLayout:
mobile/
  app/  (expo-router screens)
  components/
  lib/api.ts
  app.json
api/
  app/
  tests/
conventions: Old app versions stay in use for months: the API never breaks a released client
Screens read through a cache layer so they work offline

adrs.title: Cross-platform app
adrs.decision: One Expo codebase for iOS and Android.
adrs.why: One team ships both platforms; native modules only where needed.

adrs.title: The API keeps old clients working
adrs.decision: API versions are additive; breaking changes get a new route.
adrs.why: Store releases cannot be forced on every phone.
